name: Edogawa
tagline: Tokyo in 46 minutes and Otemachi in 47 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000.
summary: The station is in Edogawa City, served by Keisei Main Line. Journey times to the main business districts are 47 minutes to Otemachi, 58 minutes to Shinjuku, 66 minutes to Shibuya and 60 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000. The station stands 2.9 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 6.5 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 2.9 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 1.5 m to 8 m, a difference of 6.5 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 3 to 5 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 5 also fall inside the area, and the deepest projection is 3 to 5 m. For storm surge, 4 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the small side for the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 3 clinics and 2 pharmacies. The nearest hospital is 仁生社江戸川病院, about 18 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 国立国府台医療センター, about 22 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Keisei Main Line.
congestion: Keisei Main Line runs at 137% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 大神宮下→京成船橋, which this station is not on. At 100%, the ministry's scale describes every passenger either seated or able to hold a strap or pillar. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥70,000 to ¥80,000 and 1K ¥70,000 to ¥80,000. 1LDK ¥130,000 to ¥140,000 and 2LDK ¥150,000 to ¥160,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥70,000 to ¥80,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the high side. schools and parks within walking distance and quiet surroundings pushes the figure up. On the other side, only one line, the {line}, serving the station and little daily shopping within walking distance holds it down. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Keisei-Koiwa is ahead on how easy the shopping is, but Edogawa is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection.
neighbours.note: About 1 km from Edogawa in a straight line. It is served by the same lines as Edogawa. To Toranomon, for instance, Keisei-Koiwa is 3 minutes quicker. On how easy the shopping is, Keisei-Koiwa comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: Koiwa is ahead on how close the centre is and the number of medical facilities, but Edogawa is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection and quiet.
neighbours.note: About 1.5 km from Edogawa in a straight line. Koiwa has the JR Chuo-Sobu Line (Local), a different set from Edogawa. To Tokyo, for instance, Koiwa is 19 minutes quicker. On how easy the shopping is, Koiwa comes out ahead.

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 2 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 2 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: Only the Keisei Main Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the high side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are lightly loaded in the morning.
